subject: Procurement readiness & commercial path — PO vs card / marketplace interest
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>, Lauren Kim <lauren.kim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + procurement path (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Sam & Lauren,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on procurement readiness and the commercial path:

What we covered
- Use case: embed LLM into clinician workflow for triage summaries.
- Expected start: pilot Q4 (small cohort), production H1 2027.
- Key requirements: SOC 2 evidence, SSO + SCIM, invoice/PO support, data residency note.

Open items / asks for Acme Health
1) Procurement preference: PO (net30) vs corporate card for initial pilot (Sam, you mentioned PO is common) — can you confirm?
2) Marketplace interest: are you open to procuring via GCP marketplace or AWS marketplace (would simplify procurement)?
3) Approver list: who is the finance/procurement approver and do you have a standard vendor onboarding packet we should fill?
4) Timeline: rough target for PO issuance / vendor onboarding (weeks).

Attachments: attached a one-page SOW draft and the pricing sheet for the pilot for your review.

Next steps (proposed)
- If PO: please send PO template or point to the finance contact — Marissa/Rachel will push the SOW & invoice once we have PO template.
- If card for POC: we can enable a card payment up to $5k to accelerate proof-of-concept.
- Weekly quick sync (15m) until PO is in flight — propose Tuesdays 9am PT starting Aug 24.

Let me know which path you prefer and share the vendor contact for contracts/procurement. Happy to jump on a quick call with your procurement team if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf (PDF, 28 KB)]
[Attachment: Pricing-sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 14 KB)]

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Lauren Kim <lauren.kim@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement path (PO vs card / marketplace)

Thanks Marissa — good notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement preference: We prefer PO / net30 for enterprise purchases. For an initial POC we can do a corporate card charge if the amount is under $5k, as you suggested.
- Marketplace: Procurement is hesitant to use marketplaces for now (internal reasons), but platform team open to exploring later. So primary path is PO.
- Approvers: Will need Finance (Ben O'Neill), Legal (Priya Shah) and IT Security sign-off. I will introduce Ben on the thread once I confirm availability.
- Timeline: realistic procurement timeline is ~3-4 weeks once vendor packet + PO template are in hand.

I attached our PO template and vendor onboarding checklist — Lauren can confirm if anything else is required.

Sam
Sam Patel
Director, Clinical Ops | Acme Health
sam.patel@acmehealth.com

Action items from our side:
- I will populate your PO template with the pilot pricing and return as a draft (target: EOD Wed Aug 19).

- Vivek will provide a brief how-to for an initial card payment path (if you want to go that route for POC).

I'll book a 15m weekly cadence for Tuesdays 9am PT starting Aug 24 — if that doesn't work please suggest alternatives.

From: Lauren Kim <lauren.kim@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement path (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Marissa / Sam — quick procurement notes from my side:

- Confirmed: Acme prefers PO / net30 for pilots that will convert to enterprise. Card is OK for a short, limited POC (<= $5k).
- Approvals: Finance (Ben O'Neill) -> Legal (Priya Shah) -> IT Security (must confirm SOC 2/SSO).
- Documents we need from vendor: W-9, SOC 2 report (or SOC 2 Type II summary), standard MSFT/CISO security questionnaire if available, and a contact for invoicing.
- Invoice terms: net30. Please include a pricing breakout (pilot unit counts, per-seat or per-request pricing, one-time setup if any).

I've uploaded our PO template — feel free to fill and return. I'll try to get Ben and Priya on a short review thread this week.

Lauren Kim
Procurement Manager | Acme Health
lauren.kim@acmehealth.com
